title: Eye injury or chemical exposure
reference: NASA ISS Medical Operations: Ophthalmic Trauma & Chemical Hazard Decontamination Protocol.

q1.text: Was the eye exposed to chemical liquid, ammonia coolant, or toxic battery/propellant aerosol?

i_chem_flush.text: IMMEDIATE EMERGENCY EYE IRRIGATION: Connect Eye Wash Kit to potable water supply. Hold eyelids open and flush eye continuously. Activate water suction to capture floating droplets in microgravity.

t_flush.text: Flush eye continuously for 15 minutes. Check eye pH with litmus strip if available (target neutral pH 7.0–7.4).

q_chem_pain.text: Following 15 minutes of continuous irrigation, is severe ocular pain or corneal clouding persisting?

i_chem_meds.text: Instill 2 drops of Proparacaine ophthalmic anesthetic (if available) and 1 drop of broad-spectrum antibiotic drops. Apply loose protective eye patch.

end_chem_clean.text: Chemical agent thoroughly washed. Re-evaluate visual acuity; administer lubricating artificial tears.

q2.text: Is there a penetrating object, visible globe rupture, irregular pupil, or blood inside the anterior chamber (hyphema)?

i_rupture.text: CRITICAL GLOBE INJURY: DO NOT TOUCH, DO NOT REMOVE OBJECT, AND DO NOT APPLY ANY PRESSURE. Tape a rigid metallic eye shield (Fox shield) resting on orbital facial bones over the eye.

q3.text: Is there a sensation of a foreign body (dust, metal particle from EVA or maintenance), photophobia, or excessive tearing?

i_foreign_body.text: SUPERFICIAL FOREIGN BODY: Examine eyelid eversion with penlight and fluorescein strip. Irrigate gently with eye wash pouch to float particle out. If adhered, do not scrape.

i_blunt_trauma.text: BLUNT EYE CONTUSION: Apply cold compress around orbit (avoid globe pressure). Check visual acuity and extraocular muscle movement in all 4 quadrants.

end_monitor.text: Ocular irritation managed. Re-check visual acuity in 4 hours; notify Flight Surgeon if vision blurs.

end_escalate.text: OPHTHALMIC EMERGENCY ESCALATION: Flight Surgeon telemedicine consult initiated. Prepare onboard Funduscope / Slit-lamp exam.
